name: Southwest Slopes (Standard Route)
approach: Drive the Mountain Loop Highway from Darrington (WA-530) roughly 17-19.7 miles, then turn onto Forest Road 49 (Sloan Creek Road) and continue about 6.6-6.7 miles to the North Fork Sauk Trailhead (2,070 ft, vault toilet, no potable water). Hike the North Fork Sauk Trail #649 through old-growth forest, passing Red Creek camp (3.5 mi) and Mackinaw Shelter (5 mi), then climbing roughly 3,000 ft over the final miles to the Pacific Crest Trail junction (~8.2 mi from the trailhead). Turn right (southbound) on the PCT and follow it about 0.7 mi to White Pass, then continue about 2 more miles on the PCT to Indian Pass (~4,962-5,000 ft), the low point/junction with the Indian Creek Trail and the jumping-off point for the peak. Total one-way approach to Indian Pass is roughly 10.9-11 miles.

road.name: Mountain Loop Highway to Forest Road 49 (Sloan Creek Road)
road.status: Open (Mountain Loop Highway reopened mid-May 2026 after a landslide closure near milepost 37.5 that had blocked all access to FR 49 and the North Fork Sauk/Sloan Creek trails over the 2025-2026 closure period)
road.driveNote: From Darrington Ranger Station, drive the Mountain Loop Highway roughly 17-19.7 miles, turn onto FR 49 (Sloan Creek Road), and continue about 6.6-6.7 miles to the North Fork Sauk Trailhead.
road.seasonalGate: Mountain Loop Highway and FR 49 are seasonal/weather-dependent; FR 49 itself is a rough gravel road with reported washout-prone spots around mile 1 and mile 6, high-clearance recommended.

waypoints.name: North Fork Sauk Trailhead
waypoints.directions: From Darrington, drive the Mountain Loop Highway south about 16 miles to Forest Road 49 (Sloan Creek Road). Turn east and drive about 6.5 miles to the North Fork Sauk Trailhead parking at the road's end. A Northwest Forest Pass or interagency pass is required to park.
